method: instrumented scratch build of HEAD runner (phase timers on parse_event_line, add_data, engine.run, clear_data); binary reverted and rebuilt clean afterwards; clean binary verified to reproduce canonical report except timing fields
findings: For the frozen 60s decision-clock M2 variants, engine.run dominates (62%); parse is 30%; add_data ~1%.
Engine cost scales strongly with decision-clock evaluations: 1s-clock policy costs 5.5x the 60s-clock variant on the same day (82.2s vs 14.9s run).
Parse optimization can at most recover ~30% of runner wall; it cannot reach the B3 120s/day target alone.
Prepared parse path showed zero speedup earlier (dispatch/nautilus-bound) and was reverted; next B3 lever is per-evaluation policy cost on the 60s clock, measured the same way.
b3_target_status: FAIL_TARGET remains; parse work closed, nautilus/policy-level profiling is the next step
